summary: Pacific County, WA lookout site: 84-ft timber tower with L-4 cab built 1950, staffed by Florence Sanders in 1955, tower and ground house since removed, date unknown.

facts.design: 84-foot treated timber tower with 14x14 foot L-4 cab and a ground house
facts.status_note: Tower and ground house removed; the removal date is not known from the sources

staffing.status: One lookout worker named (Florence Sanders), listed late 1955

access.note: Driving ends at a gate near the Pacific/Wahkiakum county line; past it the land is private timber, and Willhite says a permit is likely required for the last mile

events.note: 84-foot treated timber tower with L-4 cab and ground house built in 1950
Florence Sanders listed at the lookout in late 1955; a September 1955 newspaper item says she was being moved to the station, spelled Blainy
Registered with Former Fire Lookout Sites on November 26, 2011 as US 1155, WA 63

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com lists Florence Sanders at the lookout in late 1955; the September 1955 newspaper item says she was being moved there. These agree closely and the story gives 1955.

notes_for_editor: Brief record checked: 2011 FFLOS registration and gone status hold up; height 25.6 m matches the 84-ft tower. The brief did not record the 1950 build or the 1955 staffing, both added. Access is set to permission from Willhite's route report, which is undated; firelookout.com and firetower.org say nothing about access. The September 6, 1955 newspaper item (Longview Daily News, as quoted on Washington Lookouts) spells the station Blainy; the story does not claim more than the item says. The newspaper names a child; the story leaves the child unnamed. WebSearch budget for this turn was exhausted by other agents, so no further sources were added.
